newsitem.title: USA: Claims from bad driving by NYC workers soar.
newsitem.headline: Claims from bad driving by NYC workers soar.

text.p: The New York City comptroller on Thursday blasted city agencies for not checking their employees' driving records, saying the workers' car accidents caused claims to soar to $30 million in fiscal year 1995.

The police department had the most unlicensed drivers with 361, followed by the fire department, which had 241. A total of 548 employees of city agencies did not have drivers' licenses, while 482 had suspended licenses and 100 had had their licenses revoked.
Further, 784 had been convicted for driving under the influence or while intoxicated, and 1,869 had had two or more accidents, the audit found.
"Effective monitoring by city agencies would keep unlicensed and unsafe drivers from getting behind the wheel and reduce the number of accidents," Hevesi said in prepared remarks.
The rise in accident claims was a 44 percent increase over the $21 million total for claims in the 1993 fiscal year.
